name: contour-agent-rules
audience: an agent generating or reviewing UI code that uses Contour
statement: Each rule names the check that enforces it, and that check is verified at build time to exist and to run in a CI lane. Rules are ordered as a working sequence: read this file, then the contracts, then write code, then run the enforcing command for what you touched. Counts are deliberately absent: the numbers an agent needs are published in contour.components.json and contour.tokens.json, which are derived from tools/lib/inventory.mjs and re-checked by their own gates, so restating one here would create a second copy of one fact. Commands assume the repository checkout, not the installed package: a consumer installs src/ and dist/ and cannot run the audit harnesses, which need a browser driver and npm-installed dependencies.

rules.rule: Edit `src/`. Everything under `dist/` is generated by `node tools/build.mjs`; a change written into `dist/` is overwritten by the next build and is not a fix.
rules.why: The package a consumer installs is derived. An edit that does not survive a rebuild is invisible.

enforcement.note: refuses a dist/ whose bytes are not what src/ produces

rules.rule: Snippets, the light-dark() fallback and every contract JSON are generated. Read them as the system's output, never hand-edit them; change the emitter or the source and regenerate.
rules.why: A generated file edited by hand is a divergence that no gate can distinguish from a fresh build until the next regeneration silently erases it.

rules.rule: Consume the token vocabulary (`var(--…)`) instead of writing a colour, duration or size literal. If the value needed does not exist, declare it in `src/css/tokens.css`.
rules.why: A literal cannot be re-themed, cannot be audited for contrast, and silently contradicts the theme the page is in.

enforcement.note: the only check that enforces this; exemptions are named ledger entries, not a regex over the whole file
the census side: every declared token is read or ledgered as unread

rules.rule: Compose existing blocks (`.c-*` with `__element` and `--variant` parts) instead of inventing a component. The names are published in `contour.components.json`.
rules.why: A class outside the contract has no states, no documentation and no contrast guarantee.

enforcement.note: the other direction: guide-only identifiers must not leak into src/

rules.rule: Every token, block or criterion named in prose must exist in the tree. Read the contracts; do not infer a name from a document.
rules.why: This repository has published a token that no stylesheet declared, and it stayed green because a gate counts declarations and a sentence is not a declaration.

enforcement.note: every url(#id) reaches a def that exists

rules.rule: Body text clears 4.5:1 and control edges, borders and focus rings clear 3:1, in both themes, against every surface a control can sit on. State is never carried by colour alone.
rules.why: The ratio is only a claim until something computes it against the surfaces it will actually render on.

enforcement.note: needs a browser driver; it exits rather than skipping without one

rules.rule: No animation runs forever without a control on the page that can stop it, and the reduced-motion path is the calm default.
rules.why: WCAG 2.2.2 is Level A, and an operating-system setting is not a control the page provides.

rules.rule: Ship no URL that points at Contour's own deployment, and no install instruction that assumes one. The project is private until v1.0 and the Pages site answers 404.
rules.why: An artifact that advertises a door nobody can open teaches the next reader to distrust the artifact.

enforcement.note: only the two $schema identifiers are permitted, and no homepage or url field

rules.rule: Import Contour by the specifier the package's `exports` map publishes (`contour-ds/contour.min.css`, `contour-ds/contour-wc.esm.js`, `contour-ds/tokens.json`, …). Never import a path under `dist/` or a fragment name the map does not define — the file may exist on disk (it is copied by `files`) and still blow up at resolution time.
rules.why: Four consumer-facing documents pointed at `contour-ds/css/ds.css` and `contour-ds/dist/wc/contour-wc-button.esm.min.js`, both of which the exports map refuses. Nothing but a resolver caught them, because `existsSync` on the installed package returns true for anything `files` copied.

enforcement.note: installs the generated tarball into every framework fixture and resolves each specifier the fixtures actually import
